Thanks for the demo earlier today — appreciate the clear walkthrough. A quick recap from our side and a few clarification questions so we can align internally before procurement: 

- High level need: Full data isolation for customer PII and transaction logs. Our security team requires that customer data must not leave our network unless explicitly encrypted/controlled.
- Primary deployment modes we're evaluating: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (single-tenant GPUs), Private VPC / on-prem (full isolation).

Questions: 
1) If we choose Dedicated capacity, can you confirm whether Redis/KV cache or other transient caches ever touch shared storage or cross-tenant hosts? We need to ensure no residual KV artifacts are accessible to other tenants.
2) For Private VPC, we assume all inference happens inside our VPC and that Redwood control plane never sees raw payloads — is that correct?
3) KMS / key ownership: do you support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own) for model payload encryption at-rest?
4) Audit logs: can we get per-request audit logs (token-level, timestamped) and are those retained in our environment for a configurable retention period?

We attached our internal security questionnaire (see attachment). If you can provide a short write-up on the differences in data handling between Dedicated vs Private VPC, that will help our InfoSec team decide which track to pursue. Ideally a short bulleted summary + any required timeline/engagement for Private.

Thanks,

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear notes and for sending the questionnaire. Summary answers below, and I included next steps at the end. Short version: Dedicated provides strong isolation at compute and tenancy level, but Private VPC (or on-prem) is the only option that guarantees no control-plane access to raw payloads.

1) Dedicated capacity
- Compute tenancy: Dedicated capacity runs on hardware reserved for your account; inference containers do not share GPU processes with other customers.
- Caching: We run prefix/KV caches in memory on the dedicated hosts. We do not persist customer KV state to shared durable storage. Cache slices are isolated to your pool by tenant ID and memory boundaries.
- Residual data: We enforce memory zeroization on container recycle; persistent artifacts (models, checkpoints) live in encrypted project-specific object stores when configured as such.

2) Private VPC / on-prem
- Inference runs entirely within your VPC or your on-prem network; the control plane (or Redwood operator) does not receive raw payloads by default. We support an optional control-plane telemetry channel that can be enabled with explicit consent.
- KMS: Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations — you retain key ownership and we never store your plaintext keys.
- Audit logs: We can ship per-request logs to your logging endpoint (CloudWatch, Splunk, GCP Stackdriver) or write to S3 buckets in your account. Retention is configurable on your side.

3) Additional notes on Hosted API
- Hosted is convenience-first; traffic passes through our hosted control plane and is logged for usage/billing. We offer encryption in transit and at rest but Hosted is not recommended when contractual data residency/isolation requirements are strict.

Next steps / proposed plan:
- I'll pull together a 1-page comparison doc (Dedicated vs Private VPC) and the Private VPC checklist (network requirements, KMS setup, onboarding timeline).
- If you prefer Private, we typically run a 4–8 week onboarding (network setup, KMS integration, validation), depending on procurement and network access windows.
- If you want a short technical call with our infra/Security lead to walk through the questionnaire answers, I can loop Rishi (SRE) and Lauren (Solutions) — would Thurs 10/16 10:00am PT or Fri 10/17 9:00am PT work?
